title: Reasons for exchange

blocks.heading: Reasons for exchange
blocks.text: Trade can connect differing resources, skills, products and markets, allowing access beyond domestic production. Benefits depend on viable costs, access and terms; reliance on a narrow product or supplier can expose livelihoods to disruption.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Use the evidence
blocks.text: Explain the trade mechanism in this fictional case: a country has surplus fish, a partner needs fish and a suitable cold-chain route exists. Trade can turn surplus into receipts and meet the partner’s demand; the cold chain makes the exchange feasible.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Several reasons for international trade
blocks.text: Natural resources and climate differ, so countries can obtain products unavailable locally. Different skills and equipment make some goods cheaper or better suited to production elsewhere. Specialising can allow larger-scale production and lower average costs when demand is sufficient. Producers can reach more buyers beyond a small domestic market. Consumers and firms can obtain a wider variety of goods, services and productive inputs. These are different benefits, but transport costs, unreliable suppliers or dependence on one export can reduce them. Explain the particular benefit and its condition rather than treating every import as a loss.
